newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAEL'S NEEMAN WITHDRAWS BUDGET CUT PROPOSAL.
newsitem.headline: ISRAEL'S NEEMAN WITHDRAWS BUDGET CUT PROPOSAL.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman on Sunday withdrew from the parliamentary finance committee a proposal to cut the 1997 budget by 800 million shekels, parliamentary officials said.

Neeman withdrew the proposal at the last minute when it became clear it was not going to pass. The cut has already been approved by the cabinet and is in addition to seven billion shekels in cuts and revenue raising measures approved earlier this year.
Officials said he planned to reintroduce it at a later date.

"The finance minister needs to do some soul-searching with regard to his relationship with the Knesset (parliament) finance committee and learn what to pass and how," said legislator Ophir Pines of the Labour party.
Members of the Shaas and National Religious Party, both coalition parties, said they opposed any attempt to cut the education and social welfare budgets.
"If coalition members won't support the government then I have nothing to do here," Neeman told reporters.
